pr_title: fix(ivy): error when accessing NgModuleRef.componentFactoryResolver in constructor
pr_body:
Currently we resolve the `NgModuleRef.componentFactoryResolver` by going through the injector, but the problem is that `ComponentFactoryResolver` has a dependency on `NgModuleRef`, which means that if the module that's attached to the ref tries to inject  `ComponentFactoryResolver` in its constructor, we'll create a circular dependency which throws at runtime.

These changes resolve the issue by creating the `ComponentFactoryResolver` manually ahead of time without going through the injector. We can do this safely, because the only dependency for the resolver is the current module ref which is providing it.

Aside from fixing the issue, another advantage to this approach is that it should reduce the amount of generated JS, because it removes a getter and a provider definition.

Fixes #35580.
pr_comments:
@crisbeto Did you try to create the component using the factory itself? (not the testbed)

The problem that I see is in [line 56](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/35637/files#diff-44fd0871b4117393a79ffaa1bb998e2aR56):

```
 this._r3Injector = createInjector(`  ...
```

Assume you are creating the module-ref for `AppModule` and an import module in `AppModule` (let call it M) requests an injection of `NgModuleRef` which internally will try to create a component using the component factory resolver.

The module-ref for `AppModule` will do

```
 this._r3Injector = createInjector(`  ...
```

Which will instantiate the other modules, including module M... at that point the constructor for module M will run and try to call `create()` on the component factory created by the resolver.

This will throw an error because the first call we are still in (`createInjector`) still did not return, having null in `_r3Injector` thus throwing [HERE](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/f95b8ce07e71cf0b736cec1f617349a44e41f939/packages/core/src/render3/component_ref.ts#L139-L141)

Since the `ComponentFactory` of `Render3` requires injections from the root view injector (`_r3Injector`) which is still not in place...

I hope i'm clear, not sure at all I am... but just gave it a shot.

I think you are solving the technical issue of having the component resolver instance but the underlying issue is the 2 phase process where we first create the core inject tokens required and then proceed to creating other modules.... i.e. the module ref for the app root must have a view injector in place before going to init other modules.
It seems to work when injecting the `ComponentFactoryResolver` as well. If you have a repo somewhere I can try out the solution against it.

@crisbeto I guess I'll wait for the release to check it with a complex scenario like I have in my library.

I'll update when and if I find something. Thank you!

issue_context.title: [IVY]: Fail to get `componentFactoryResolver` from a child NgModuleRef
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/core ### Is this a regression? Worked in 8 and below ### Description When trying to access `componentFactoryResolver` on an instance of `NgModuleRef` that is not the root module there is an exception thrown:
TypeError: Cannot read property 'get' of undefined

at NgModuleRef$1.get (core.umd.js:24253) at NgModuleRef$1.get [as componentFactoryResolver] (core.umd.js:24257) at new FeatModule (feat-module.ts:8) at Object.FeatModule_Factory [as factory] (feat-module.ts:12) at R3Injector.hydrate (core.umd.js:11505) at R3Injector.get (core.umd.js:11328) at eval (core.umd.js:11268) at Set.forEach () at new R3Injector (core.umd.js:11268) at createInjector (core.umd.js:11233)

The issue is that there is no value in the `_r3Injector` property... it exists only in the root module. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Go to https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-9-abstract-g6cugw?file=src%2Fapp%2Ffeat-module%2Ffeat-module.ts There is a debugger statement in line 22, the issue will throw in line 24. ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 9.0.2
Node: 12.9.1
OS: darwin x64

Angular: 9.0.1
... animations, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, elements
... forms, language-service, platform-browser
... platform-browser-dynamic, platform-server, router
Ivy Workspace: Yes

rxjs                                       6.5.4
typescript                                 3.7.5
webpack                                    4.41.2
Also worth noting, that if requesting an injection of `ComponentFactoryResolver` it is totally fine. You get an instance of `ComponentFactoryResolver` that points to it's `NgModuleRef` (`ngModule` prop) and that `NgModuleRef` will **NOT** point to that `ComponentFactoryResolver` we just got... it will throw when trying to access it's `componentFactoryResolver ` property.
